questions.q: What does the "Remote Call-In" pattern describe?
options: A screen updating automatically when data changes
Salesforce calling out and waiting for a response
An external system calling into Salesforce synchronously to read or write data
A batch job syncing data overnight
questions.explain: Remote Call-In is the pattern name for inbound integration — an external system synchronously calling into Salesforce, covered in Chapter 2.

questions.q: Which pattern fits a scenario where Salesforce calls out and must wait for the answer before continuing, because the next step depends on it?
options: Batch Data Synchronization
Remote Call-In
Fire and Forget
Request-Reply
questions.explain: Request-Reply is specifically the synchronous pattern where Salesforce holds state and waits for the remote system's response before proceeding.

questions.q: Which Salesforce mechanisms are typically used to implement the Batch Data Synchronization pattern?
options: Batch Apex combined with Scheduled Apex
Platform Events and Change Data Capture
Outbound Messaging only
Apex REST and the webservice keyword
questions.explain: Batch Data Synchronization is implemented with Batch Apex for scoped chunk processing, often triggered on a timer by Scheduled Apex.

questions.q: What is the key idea this lesson emphasizes about a pattern name like "Fire and Forget"?
options: It refers to one single, specific Apex class that must always be used
It describes the shape of a requirement, not a specific piece of code or feature — several different mechanisms could implement the same pattern
It only applies to SOAP-based integrations
It is interchangeable with Request-Reply
questions.explain: A pattern name describes the requirement's shape (synchronous vs asynchronous, etc.); which specific mechanism implements it is a separate decision covered in Lesson 20.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that naming integration patterns is valuable, even though no new Salesforce feature is introduced?
options: Because it replaces the need for Named Credentials
Because it unlocks additional governor limits
Because a shared vocabulary lets architects and developers communicate a requirement's shape quickly and precisely, the same way naming a software design pattern does
Because pattern names are required by Salesforce's terms of service
questions.explain: The value is purely communicative — a shared vocabulary that speeds up design discussions, similar to naming a classic software design pattern.
